key_insight: A coherent Ising machine can accelerate Bayesian MAP inference for tokamak plasma parameter inversion by mapping the negative log-posterior to a spin Hamiltonian and searching it via optical bifurcation dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This offers a potential path to near-real-time fusion plasma control by reducing the computational bottleneck of nonlinear multi-diagnostic data assimilation.
method: Formulate plasma inference as a MAP optimization problem under a nonlinear Gaussian likelihood.
Encode the negative log-posterior into a CIM spin model using coupled DOPOs with all-to-all connectivity.
Use a block-coordinate iterative scheme to handle problem size beyond current hardware limits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports validation on EAST tokamak plasma current profile inversion with an approximately 1 ms single-run solution time.
watch_item: Current qubit/hardware limits require block-wise iteration, so the method is not yet fully real-time for large-scale deployment.
paper_title: Solving Large-Scale Parameter Inference in Controllable Nuclear Fusion via Coherent Ising Machines and Block Coordinate Descent
